claim.operational_target: Determine whether a rank-3 support-set generator improves held-out synthetic-person binary choice NLL over both personal MAP logistic and person-embedding MLP baselines.
non_claims: Generated weights are the person's mind, values, personality, or mechanism.
Synthetic performance transfers to real people.
A low-rank adapter identifies a causal psychological process.
alternatives: Personal MAP logistic is sufficient and more stable.
Any apparent gain is support/test leakage, person-ID memorization, or order dependence.
claim.scope: Synthetic held-out people in one five-feature binary-choice task; support sizes 0, 16, 32, and 64; scenario test is primary, temporal test secondary, OOD diagnostic only.

identifiability.distinguishing_evidence: Support-only generated heads are scored on disjoint answers for unseen people against fixed population, personal MAP, and embedding baselines across five seeds.

evidence.completeness_boundary: Synthetic generation is complete by construction; real collection requires an external registry and trusted chronology.

computation.deployment_kernel: The generated weight vector is deployed through LogisticChoiceModel.probabilities, the same kernel used by baseline reports.
computation.selection_kernel: Validation people select only the epoch from a preregistered rank-3, 80-epoch candidate path.
computation.uncertainty_scope: Five deterministic seeds and paired point NLL differences; no real-person confidence interval.
